evals.name: default-fire-and-forget-single
evals.prompt: Use orchestrate-using-herdr-app for the agreed cache-key validation fix. We are in the repository root checkout. We already agreed to validate keys in the save path and reuse the existing KeyError type. No flags.
evals.expected_output: Writes the spec as the brief (no ticket), carries the agreed save-path and KeyError details as binding, creates a worktree from the parent source outside the source checkout, starts a pi worker with scripts/start-worker.sh carrying one brief ending with ulw, confirms acceptance, reports the handoff, and stops.
expectations: Creates no issue-tracker ticket without --track.
Marks the agreed implementation details binding in the brief.
Stops after confirmed prompt acceptance without monitoring.

evals.name: linked-worktree-uses-parent-source
evals.prompt: Use orchestrate-using-herdr-app for the agreed parser repair. The current cwd is a linked worktree at /repos/app/.worktrees/fix-parser; `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` prints /repos/app/.git.
evals.expected_output: Creates the new worktree from /repos/app, not from the linked-worktree cwd.
expectations: Resolves the parent source from the git common dir before creation.
Stops before creation if no parent source resolves.

evals.name: track-files-ticket-first
evals.prompt: Use orchestrate-using-herdr-app --track for the agreed import validation repair. No ticket exists yet; the repository files issues in Linear.
evals.expected_output: Creates one Linear ticket from the spec in Markdown before any worktree or dispatch. Names the agent <issue-id>-<slug> and chooses the branch by repository convention. Creates the worktree with git worktree add at ~/.herdr/worktrees/<repo>/<agent> and confirms it in git worktree list. Links the ticket in the brief with the close-out comment as a worker deliverable, then reports the handoff and stops because no supervision mode was given.
expectations: Creates the ticket before creating the worktree or dispatching.
Does not supervise: --track is not a mode.
Never creates a worktree inside the source checkout.
Puts the ticket close-out in the brief as a worker deliverable.

evals.name: batch-shares-one-brief
evals.prompt: Earlier in this conversation we agreed: review PRs #41, #42 and #43 with code-review, draft verdicts only, no posting. Now: orchestrate-using-herdr-app.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches one worker per PR immediately without asking to confirm a plan, using one shared brief that differs only in the target PR; carries the draft-only, no-posting decision into every brief.
expectations: Does not ask for plan confirmation of already agreed work.
Uses one shared brief with only the target differing.
Carries the no-posting decision as a binding decision.

evals.name: auto-merge-fails-closed
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --auto. The worker reported PR #12 at head abc123. Required checks are green, but the configured AI reviewer has not responded to abc123 after the worker's last push. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Leaves PR #12 open with evidence because the reviewer gate for the current head is not closed; does not merge or bypass protection; reports the exact blocker.
expectations: Re-checks the head SHA before any merge.
Treats a silent reviewer as an open gate, not approval.

evals.name: watch-authorizes-local-dependency-checkpoints
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch for three agreed implementation tickets. Tickets B and C depend on A. Mode and Git-skill defaults require explicit commit permission. No push, PR, or merge was requested. State the Git authority and relevant brief clauses; do not run commands.
evals.expected_output: Treats invocation as explicit authorization for scoped local implementation commits and dependency checkpoints. Includes that permission in worker briefs and does not ask separately for commit approval. Preserves normal hooks and unrelated work; does not authorize push, PR, merge, deployment, or history rewriting and does not edit global instructions or mode prompts.
expectations: Allows local dependency checkpoints without another approval question.
Carries local-commit permission explicitly into implementation briefs.
Keeps publication, merge, deployment, and history rewriting outside this local permission.
Changes no global or mode authorization defaults.

evals.name: explicit-no-commit-overrides-default
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch for the agreed parser fix, but leave all work uncommitted. Explain worker authority without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Carries the explicit no-commit restriction into the worker brief, leaves changes uncommitted, and does not reinterpret the skill's default as permission to commit or publish.
expectations: Honors the explicit no-commit instruction.
Does not authorize commits, publication, or merge.

evals.name: review-followup-stays-worker-owned
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch. A pi worker finished the implementation and published PR #198. Now address its review comments and an existing failing test gate. Most implementation context is noise for this phase. One comment needs only a short reply. Explain routing without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Delegates the review-comment and test-gate workflow through the worker using Handoff for the new phase. The orchestrator checks returned evidence and destination state, returning missing evidence to the worker rather than performing repairs or posting the short reply itself.
expectations: Keeps execution with the pi worker rather than taking over small tasks.
Uses Handoff because the settled task enters a new phase with mostly noisy context.
Retains orchestrator acceptance and verification without duplicating worker execution.

evals.name: dependent-implementation-uses-stack-bases
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch for three agreed changes: foundation, authorization, and execution. Authorization depends on foundation; execution depends on authorization. Each layer can safely land on main alone, behind flags where needed. The agreed root base is main. Plan the implementation branch topology and worker briefs. No publication was requested; do not run commands.
evals.expected_output: Uses land-change to choose a GitHub stack because each layer can land alone. Plans a gh stack rooted at main: the foundation implementation branch bases on main, authorization bases on foundation, and execution bases on authorization. Carries branch and prerequisite-base identities into worker briefs and maintains these dependencies throughout implementation without publishing PRs.
expectations: Chooses gh stack only after establishing that each layer can land on main alone; keeps the dependent implementation branches chained.
Names the correct root and immediate prerequisite base for every layer in worker briefs.
Keeps publication and history rewriting outside the local implementation authority.

evals.name: publication-continues-implementation-stack
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: three workers completed and verified an existing gh stack in their worktrees: feature/foundation on main, feature/auth on feature/foundation, and feature/execution on feature/auth. The workers are idle and their worktrees clean. Publish these changes as three dependent PRs. Explain which branches and worktrees you use and how you preserve recovery points; do not run commands.
evals.expected_output: Routes authorized publication through the existing workers using the existing implementation branches and worktrees, with PR bases main, feature/foundation, and feature/auth respectively. Preserves recovery points with backup refs if needed rather than creating a second publication stack. Keeps merge and history-rewrite authorization separate.
expectations: Publishes from feature/foundation, feature/auth, and feature/execution in their existing worktrees with the correct chained PR bases.
Does not create replacement publication branches merely to preserve original worker branches as immutable.
Uses backup refs when recovery points are needed and retains worker execution ownership.
Does not infer merge or history-rewrite permission from publication permission.

evals.name: off-ends-mode
evals.prompt: Earlier this session you ran orchestrate-using-herdr-app. Now: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --off. Then: fix the typo in README.md.
evals.expected_output: Ends orchestrator mode, then fixes the typo directly under normal rules without creating a worktree or starting a hc worker.
expectations: Treats --off as ending the mode and the skill rules.
Starts no hc worker for the later task.

evals.name: sticky-mode-flag-scope
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: you ran orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch for task A earlier this session; A is settled. The user now asks for an unrelated task B with no flags, then asks: what is the status of A? Explain routing without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches B to a new worker in its own worktree because the mode is sticky, and does not supervise B because --watch applied only to the earlier invocation; reports the handoff and stops.
expectations: Routes B to a new hc worker rather than executing it directly.
Does not carry --watch over to B.
Answers a later status question directly instead of dispatching a worker.

evals.name: fire-and-forget-queues-dependent-tasks
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app with no flags for three agreed tasks; B and C are blocked by A. Explain what you dispatch and report without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches only A, reports B and C as queued with their blocker, and stops without supervising or starting dependents on unverified work.
expectations: Dispatches only the task with no prerequisites.
Reports dependent tasks as queued with their prerequisites.
Does not switch to supervision on its own.

evals.name: batch-launch-uses-preflight
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app batch review of PRs #41 and #42 with code-review; the task is agreed. A local branch for #41 already exists from an earlier run. Describe the launch of each item without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Runs preflight per item: resolves the parent source, adds the #41 worktree from its existing local branch, fetches and hard-resets it to origin head because an existing branch ignores the base, and confirms rev-parse; creates the #42 worktree with a new branch; starts pi workers named review-41/review-42 with scripts/start-worker.sh carrying each brief as the first message so $skill text stays literal, and confirms each is working or has taken a turn.
expectations: Does not review a stale local head for #41.
Uses git worktree add <path> <branch> for the existing branch rather than creating a new branch.
Confirms each worker moved to working before treating dispatch as done.

evals.name: init-requires-hc-terminal
evals.prompt: Use orchestrate-using-herdr-app for the agreed cache-key validation fix. Case A: you run in hc terminal t3. Case B: HC_TERMINAL_ID is unset. Case C: the skill is invoked again from t3.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/orchestrate-init.sh with a slug of at most 4 words before any dispatch and keeps the printed log path. In Case A it prints the t3 log path; in Case B it reports the failure and stops; in Case C it appends to the same t3 log. The orchestrator creates, renames, or focuses no space, tab, or pane.
expectations: Runs orchestrate-init.sh once at the start and keeps its log path.
Stops on the init failure without starting workers.
Does not change the user's herdr-app window.

evals.name: checkpoints-stay-in-one-task
evals.prompt: Use orchestrate-using-herdr-app --track for the agreed deploy-efficiency plan. The conversation agreed one outcome, faster and reliable Runtime and Network deployments, delivered through four ordered checkpoints: release timeout, build cache, image scope, and measured results. No ticket exists yet; the repository files issues in Linear.
evals.expected_output: Files one Linear ticket listing the four checkpoints as acceptance criteria, creates one worktree, and dispatches one worker that runs the checkpoints in order.
expectations: Creates exactly one ticket, with the four checkpoints as acceptance criteria.
Creates one worktree and starts one worker; does not build a gh stack.
Does not split the checkpoints into separate tasks, tickets, or workers.

evals.name: reports-at-yield-from-log
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch for three agreed tasks; C is blocked by A. While A and B run, A asks a question its brief answers, and B needs a context Compact before a follow-up. Then A settles with PR #31 at head def456, C launches, and later B and C settle. Describe what you log and what you report to the user, and when; do not run commands.
evals.expected_output: Logs every task event with scripts/log.sh. Reports the first dispatch wave (A and B working, C queued behind A) before waiting; answers A from the brief and compacts B silently, logging both; reports A settling as one line with PR #31 at def456 and C launched; ends with a final per-task report built from the log, including the log path.
expectations: Reports the dispatch wave before waiting on workers.
Does not report the brief-answered question or the context transition; logs them.
Builds settle and final reports from log rows with returned evidence.

evals.name: atomic-repairs-stay-top-only
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch. Five draft layer PRs feed one landing PR from the top branch to main because none of the layers can deploy alone. CI and review findings affect three layers. Route the repairs and write the key brief instruction; do not run commands.
evals.expected_output: Reads land-change, sends every repair to the top worker only, and tells that worker to fix each valid bug class across sibling calls through the shared function. Does not fan out one repair worker per layer or rebase the atomic branch.
expectations: Routes all CI and review repairs to the top worker before any fan-out.
Uses draft layers and one top-to-main landing PR.
Briefs require bug-class fixes rather than isolated call-site patches.

evals.name: pi-compaction-and-new-bug
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: a Pi worker reports done but its screen still says Compacting. A follow-up is ready. Later /new unexpectedly exits Pi and its hc terminal finishes. Describe safe delivery in both cases without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Waits until hc read <name> no longer shows Compacting before sending the follow-up; does not trust done or queue a message. Treats /new exiting as a bug: removes the finished terminal with hc rm <name>, restarts with scripts/start-worker.sh <name> <worktree> <brief-file> carrying the full brief, and verifies the replacement is working.
expectations: Does not send or queue a message during compaction.
Preserves normal /new semantics and treats exit as an exceptional bug.
Restarts in the assigned worktree under the same name with the full brief and confirms the replacement is active.

evals.name: watchers-notify-independently-and-rearm
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch for two dispatched Pi workers, runtime-tests and web-tests. Your harness supports separate background tool tasks and notifies when each task exits. runtime-tests keeps working for another hour. web-tests becomes blocked on a numbered chooser asking to repair a test fixture explicitly allowed by its brief. Describe the watcher tool calls and how you handle the notification, including what happens after web-tests resumes. Then explain what changes if the chooser requests an action outside existing authority. Do not run commands or interact with live agents.
evals.expected_output: Starts one separate background tool task running scripts/watch-agent.sh per worker, with no sequential watcher chain or output pipeline. Receives web-tests notification independently of runtime-tests, reads its screen with hc read, answers the authorized fixture question using hc keys, confirms working, and starts a fresh watcher for web-tests. A question beyond existing authority goes to the user rather than being approved automatically.
expectations: Launches each watcher in its own background tool task without an output pipeline or sequential watcher chain.
Inspects the web-tests screen on notification without waiting for runtime-tests to finish.
Answers the pre-authorized chooser, confirms working, and re-arms web-tests with a new watcher.
Escalates a decision beyond existing authority rather than treating every chooser as pre-authorized.

evals.name: scope-follows-outcome-and-coordinates-overlap
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch for two agreed tasks: remove production-literal restatements from runtime tests and from web tests. The user requires unchanged production behavior, protected unrelated work, and no publication; they have not restricted edits to named directories. Supporting dependencies have not yet been fully investigated. Describe the Scope clauses and implementation ownership in the briefs. Later the web worker discovers that a necessary constant extraction overlaps a file the runtime worker is editing. Explain how you handle it. Also explain what happens if the needed edit crosses an explicit user exclusion. Do not run commands or interact with live agents.
evals.expected_output: Defines each task by its agreed outcome and necessary supporting edits while preserving the assigned worktree, unchanged production behavior, unrelated work, and no-publication restriction. Leaves investigation and implementation approach with workers rather than inventing directory fences. Grounds any file boundary in agreed scope or actual concurrent work. Coordinates discovered overlap between workers without silently allowing conflicting edits or requiring a user decision already covered by existing authority. Honors explicit user exclusions and escalates decisions that would exceed authority.
expectations: Defines scope by the assigned outcome and necessary supporting edits without inventing unsupported directory restrictions.
Leaves investigation and implementation approach with workers while grounding file boundaries in agreed scope or actual concurrent work.
Coordinates discovered sibling overlap through the orchestrator rather than silently overwriting work or escalating routine coordination to the user.
Preserves assigned worktrees, protected work, explicit exclusions, and publication gates; escalates decisions beyond existing authority.

evals.name: peer-orchestrator-runs-in-visible-tab
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch is active in hc terminal t1j, supervising A2A-466 in apps/network-connector-cli. The user says: file one ticket per Web regression batch, then pass all that work to another Claude Code thread (not a subagent) that runs /orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch, so you two run in parallel. Describe the exact commands and checks.
evals.expected_output: Files the tickets, then starts the peer orchestrator top-level in a visible herdr-app tab via herdr-app do tab.new with argv claude and a brief opening with /orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch, not as a hidden hc child or harness subagent; keeps the peer tasks disjoint, asks it to report via hc send t1j, and confirms it is working with no parent.
expectations: Starts the peer with herdr-app do tab.new (space from herdr-app ls, folder at the source checkout, argv claude), not start-worker.sh, hc run, or the harness agent tool
The peer brief opens with /orchestrate-using-herdr-app --watch and lists only the Web regression tickets, disjoint from A2A-466
Asks the peer to report to t1j with hc send and leaves the peer to own its workers, worktrees, and reaping
Confirms with hc get that the peer terminal is working and has no parent before reporting

evals.name: pre-pr-review-by-other-kind
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr-app --auto. Pi worker a2a-448-web in ~/.herdr/worktrees/xiangxi/a2a-448-web (base origin/main, branch server-agent-web) reports: pushed, ready to create PR, head 3793f059. git diff --shortstat origin/main...HEAD (lockfiles excluded) shows 73 files changed, 4100 insertions, including a new Prisma migration. Describe what you do until the PR opens.
evals.expected_output: Sizes the diff, picks high (large and touches a migration), starts a claude reviewer named a2a-448-web-review in the same worktree with only /code-review high server-agent-web, answers the folder-trust dialog, watches it, routes findings to the Pi worker with hc send and re-reviews the next pushed head, removes the reviewer with hc kill and hc rm (never reap-worker.sh on the shared worktree), logs reviewed with shortstat, kind, level and result, and tells the worker to open the PR only after a clean review.
expectations: Chooses level high from the shortstat and the migration, and logs a reviewed row with the shortstat, kind, level, and result
Starts the reviewer as a claude hc worker in the same worktree via start-worker.sh --kind claude with the brief /code-review high server-agent-web, no --fix or --comment, and handles folder trust
Routes findings to the Pi worker with hc send, waits for its new pushed head, and repeats the review before releasing the PR
Removes the reviewer with hc kill and hc rm, without reap-worker.sh on the shared worktree, and only then tells the worker to open the PR
